{{Short description|Theorem in number theory}}

In [[number theory]], a [[real-valued function]] <math>f(n)</math> on the [[integer]]s is [[additive function|''additive'']] if <math>f(mn)=f(m)+f(n)</math> for coprime ''m'', ''n''.  The '''Erdős–Wintner theorem''' gives a condition under which a real-valued additive function has a limiting distribution
<math display=block>F(y)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N} \#\{n<N~:~f(n)\leqslant~y\}.</math>
In particular, it asserts that the limiting function exists if the three following series pertaining to [[prime number]]s converge:
<math display=block>\sum_{|f(p)|>1}\frac{1}{p},~~\sum_{f(p)\leqslant1}\frac{f(p)}{p},~~\sum_{|f(p)|\leqslant1}\frac{f(p)^2}{p}.</math>
When this happens, the [[Characteristic function (probability theory)|characteristic function]] <math>v(t)</math> of the limiting distribution <math>F</math> is equal to
<math display=block>v(t)=\prod_{p}\left(1-\frac{1}{p}\right)\left(1+\sum^{\infin}_{m=1}p^{-m}\exp(itf(p^m))\right),</math>
where <math>i</math> is the [[imaginary unit]]. Furthermore, the limiting distribution is [[continuous function|continuous]] if and only if the series
<math display=block>\sum_{f(p)\neq0}\frac{1}{p}</math>
diverges, otherwise the distribution is purely discrete.<ref>{{Citation |last=Elliott |first=P. D. T. A. |chapter=The Erdös — Wintner Theorem |date=1979 |title=Probabilistic Number Theory I: Mean-Value Theorems |pages=187–224 |editor-last=Elliott |editor-first=P. D. T. A. |place=New York, NY |publisher=Springer |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-1-4612-9989-9_6 |isbn=978-1-4612-9989-9 }}</ref>
It is an analogue in [[probabilistic number theory]] of [[Kolmogorov's three-series theorem]].

The condition that <math>f(n)</math> is additive can be rephrased as
<math display=block>f(p_1^{e^1}\cdots~p_r^{e^r}) = f(p_1^{e^1})+\cdots+f(p_r^{e^r})</math>
where <math>e_1,\ldots,e_r</math> represent the positive integers, and <math>p_1,\ldots,p_r</math> represent distinct primes.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Drmota |first=Michael |last2=Verwee |first2=Johann |date=2021-12-01 |title=Effective Erdős–Wintner theorems for digital expansions |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022314X2100144X |journal=Journal of Number Theory |volume=229 |pages=218–260 |doi=10.1016/j.jnt.2021.04.006 |issn=0022-314X}}</ref>
